atoms.canonical_statement: The study aimed to identify clinical features of recurrent Guillain-Barré syndrome in a large cohort of adult GBS patients.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the aim was to identify clinical features of RGBS in a large cohort of adult GBS patients.

atoms.canonical_statement: Over six years, 404 patients with GBS were hospitalized at seven tertiary centers in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina (Republic of Srpska), and Montenegro.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: During a 6-year period, 404 GBS patients were hospitalized in seven tertiary health care centers of three Balkan countries: Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina (Republic of Srpska), and Montenegro.

population.label: GBS cohort hospitalized at seven tertiary centers in three Balkan countries

atoms.canonical_statement: GBS diagnosis required fulfillment of the standard National Institute of Neurological Diseases and Stroke criteria.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The diagnosis of GBS was made if patients fulfilled the standard National Institute of Neurological Diseases and Stroke (NINDS) criteria.

population.label: Patients meeting standard NINDS diagnostic criteria for GBS

atoms.canonical_statement: GBS subtypes were assigned using clinical and electrophysiological findings.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A definitive diagnosis of GBS subtypes was made according to the clinical and electrophysiological findings.

atoms.canonical_statement: Sociodemographic and clinical variables for current and previous episodes were obtained from medical records.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Sociodemographic and clinical data (including age, gender, preceding factors, functional disability at nadir and on discharge, cerebrospinal fluid analysis, and therapeutic modalities) were obtained from medical records for actual and previous episodes.

atoms.canonical_statement: Functional disability was graded with the GBS disability scale from 0 to 6; scores greater than 3 were defined as severe disability.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The GDS ranges from 0 (no symptoms) to 6 (lethal outcome), where >3 was defined as a severe disability.

outcome.definition: Scale ranges from 0 (no symptoms) to 6 (lethal outcome); >3 was defined as severe disability.

atoms.canonical_statement: Recurrent GBS was defined according to suggestions by Kuitwaard et al.; the criteria were referenced rather than restated in the article.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: RGBS was defined according to suggestions by Kuitwaard et al.

atoms.canonical_statement: The analysis used descriptive statistics including mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, and maximum.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In this study, methods of descriptive statistics were used including mean, standard deviation, median, minimum and maximum.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Therapeutic plasma exchange (PLEx) was admitted in 23.1% of patients during the first attack and it was not administered during the second attack of GBS.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors proposed that greater IVIg/plasma-exchange use during recurrent episodes may partly explain why recurrent attacks were not more disabling.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: It is possible that our patients did not have more severe disability during the second GBS episode since they received IVIg/PLEx therapy more frequently during the recurrent episode.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that recurrent GBS occurred in about 3% of the cohort, nearly one-quarter changed variant at the second attack, disability was similar across attacks, and immunomodulatory therapy was used more often during recurrent GBS.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Although GBS is generally a monophasic disease, around 3% of our patients with GBS have already had a episode of GBS. Almost one-quarter of our patients presented with a different variant during the second GBS attack. The degree of disability was similar during the first and the recurrent episode of the disease, but immunomodulatory therapy was more frequently applied during RGBS.
